column1: # boru Language Specification: the boru:fmt module
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# The source pretty-printer, exposed as a runtime API. Fmt.format formats
# boru source text into canonical layout (normalised spacing, a trailing
# newline) and shares its implementation with the `boru fmt` CLI. The result
# is the formatted string, so the expected column is the canonical
# single-quoted rendering with the trailing newline shown as \n.
# The non-concrete-argument error arm is pinned by a Go test
# (lang/go/modules/fmt_test.go) rather than an ERROR row here.
import "boru:fmt" end Fmt.format "[ a  b  c ]"
column3: Fmt.format collapses list spacing and adds a trailing newline

column1: import "boru:fmt" end Fmt.format "{ a:1   b:2 }"
column3: Fmt.format normalises map spacing

column1: import "boru:fmt" end Fmt.format "def x 1"
column3: Fmt.format keeps canonical source but ensures a trailing newline

column1: import "boru:fmt" end Fmt.format "def double fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [x mul 2]]"
column3: Fmt.format drops brackets around a single fn param and return

column1: import "boru:fmt" end Fmt.format "def   f   (+re/[a-z]+/)"
column3: Fmt.format keeps a minilang literal verbatim (its [ ] + delimiters are not re-tokenised) while normalising the surrounding spacing

column1: import "boru:fmt" end Fmt.format "+gex|a*b|"
column3: Fmt.format leaves a pipe-delimited minilang literal untouched

column1: import "boru:fmt" end Fmt.format "size none"
column3: Fmt.format keeps the lowercase none VALUE verbatim (never rewrites it to the None type)

column1: import "boru:fmt" end Fmt.format "list 1 2 3"
column3: Fmt.format keeps the list constructor word verbatim (never rewrites it to the List type)

column1: import "boru:fmt" end Fmt.format "x is integer"
column3: Fmt.format still capitalises a genuine lowercase type name

column1: import "boru:fmt" end Fmt.format "def sum3 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer c:Integer] [Integer] [a add b add c]] end sum3 1 2 3"
column2: 'def sum3 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer c:Integer] [Integer] [a add b add c]]\n  ; sum3 1 2 3\n'
column3: Fmt.format never drops statements that trail a fn definition (no truncation); the terminator normalises to `;` (STYLE-GUIDE §S6)

column1: import "boru:fmt" end Fmt.format-markdown "```boru\ndef  x  1\n```"
column3: Fmt.format-markdown reformats a fenced boru block

column1: import "boru:fmt" end Fmt.format-html "<!-- borufmt -->\ndef  z   3\n<!-- /borufmt -->"
column3: Fmt.format-html reformats a marker region, leaving the rest

column1: import "boru:fmt" end Fmt.render 40 {fmt:"group" body:{fmt:"concat" parts:["a" {fmt:"line"} "b"]}}
column3: Fmt.render lays a doc flat when it fits the width

column1: import "boru:fmt" end Fmt.render 1 {fmt:"group" body:{fmt:"concat" parts:["a" {fmt:"line"} "b"]}}
column3: Fmt.render breaks a doc that does not fit the width

column1: import "boru:fmt" end Fmt.render 20 {fmt:'indent' by:-1 body:{fmt:'concat' parts:[{fmt:'hardline'} 'x']}}
column3: a NEGATIVE document indent clamps to column 0 (no strings.Repeat panic — PR #298 review P1)

column1: # The XSLT-style rule vocabulary: Fmt.kind supplies a node's dispatch key
# (an XSLT match pattern) and Fmt.children its child sequence
# (apply-templates' node list). Both are pure value->value transforms, so a
# declarative rule table + a four-line apply driver — the whole formatter —
# is ordinary boru (see the end-to-end loop in modules/fmtrule_test.go).
import "boru:fmt" end {a:1} Fmt.kind
column3: Fmt.kind classifies an untagged Map as 'map'

column1: import "boru:fmt" end [1 2] Fmt.kind
column3: Fmt.kind classifies a List as 'list'

column1: import "boru:fmt" end 5 Fmt.kind
column3: Fmt.kind classifies a scalar leaf as 'scalar'

column1: import "boru:fmt" end {$kind:'entry' key:'a'} Fmt.kind
column3: Fmt.kind reports a $kind-tagged Map's own tag

column1: import "boru:fmt" end {a:1 b:2} Fmt.children
column3: Fmt.children yields one entry node per Map key

column1: import "boru:fmt" end [7 8] Fmt.children
column3: Fmt.children yields a List's elements verbatim

column1: import "boru:fmt" end 5 Fmt.children
column3: Fmt.children yields no children for a scalar leaf

column1: # Fmt.tree bridges boru SOURCE into the same $kind-tagged value tree, so the
# rule vocabulary can format real code, not just data (see the declarative
# source formatter in modules/fmttree_test.go).
import "boru:fmt" end Fmt.kind (Fmt.tree "x")
column3: Fmt.tree parses source into a $kind-tagged CST whose root node classifies as 'root'

column1: import "boru:fmt" end (((Fmt.tree "foo") get "children") get 0) get "text"
column3: Fmt.tree exposes each node's text and children, so a rule set can walk real boru source

column1: # The declarative rule table: Fmt.rules exposes the canonical layout
# stylesheet as boru data; Fmt.format-with formats under a (partial)
# override table. Rules are DATA and the emitter is the processor that
# interprets them (the XSLT split); whitespace — attachment, indent,
# width, fill-wrapping — is owned by the rules, which is why overriding
# them changes it and why the canonical table reproduces Fmt.format
# byte-for-byte (the authority row below).
import "boru:fmt" end (Fmt.rules) get "width"
column3: the canonical rule table carries the 72-column width as data

column1: import "boru:fmt" end Fmt.format-with {} "def  x  1"
column3: an empty override table formats with the canonical rules

column1: import "boru:fmt" end eq (Fmt.format-with (Fmt.rules) "a, b; c") (Fmt.format "a, b; c")
column3: the boru rule table is AUTHORITATIVE: feeding Fmt.rules back reproduces Fmt.format

column1: import "boru:fmt" end Fmt.format-with {width:20} "[alpha bravo charlie delta]"
column3: width is a rule: 20 columns wraps the list with the greedy fill

column1: import "boru:fmt" end Fmt.format-with {attach:{comma:'none'}} "a, b"
column3: attachment is a rule: detaching comma spaces it like any word

column1: import "boru:fmt" end Fmt.format-with {templates:{list:['<' apply/q '>']}} "[1 2]"
column3: a TEMPLATE override: the literals around the apply/q recursion op are the list's brackets

column1: import "boru:fmt" end ((Fmt.rules) get "templates") get "list"
column3: the canonical list template — literals around the recursion op, the XSLT-template analogue

column1: import "boru:fmt" end Fmt.format-with {strategies:['bogus']} "a"
column3: an unknown statement strategy is rejected, not silently ignored

column1: import "boru:fmt" end Fmt.format-with {widht:72} "a"
column3: a misspelled rule key is rejected (typo protection)

column1: import "boru:fmt" end Fmt.format-with {width:'x'} "a"
column3: a non-integer width is rejected

column1: import "boru:fmt" import "boru:minilang" end (Fmt.tree "def x 1") mini sp 'count(//children)' {}
column3: sp (structure-path) selects into the Fmt.tree CST — the path minilang over boru structure
